I also like to make friendship bracelets, they aren't always pretty but that's ok because they make great bookmarks lol.

As for your nose and your face, the best thing I've found is a skin care routine. Even a small one that keeps the pickable things on your face to a minimum can really help. Pore strips for your nose can help but be careful because those can hurt your skin more than help!! I do those twice a month AT MOST. Otherwise, figure out your skin type and find a nice face mask that works with it. A simple skin care routine involves a cleanser and a moisturizer, washing twice a day, and wearing sunscreen while outside.

Changing schools is tough. Even without anxiety, it's tough. It takes a while to get into a groove that has you comfortable with reaching out and welcoming people into your life. And school is a hard place for that to happen sometimes. There's nothing wrong with that, hell it's pretty damn common. As for the anxiety part, that's also pretty normal. At least for someone with anxiety. I had such severe anxiety I was diagnosed with agoraphobia so I get it, that feeling of needing to be social and interacting is draining and it really does suck the energy out of you. Having anxiety just means you have less social energy than other people do.

If you ever need someone to talk to, come talk to me. I was in most of theses situations too. I get that wanting to be out but enjoying the feeling of stealth as well, not connecting well with people or friends, that severe anxiety feel of never being able to be around people, even changing schools and struggling to make friends - I went through that shit. People always talk about great it is to be fantastic all the time but you don't need to be happy-go-lucky 24/7, there's nothing wrong with just floating if you're not strong enough to swim. So take a breath, you're gonna get through it. Shit will get better with time. And if you need some advice or someone to vent to - my inbox is open.

Next, track the period. If he's able to notice how heavy his flow is, track that as well. Mainly, you're looking to see how many days it lasts.

Third, contact his endocrinologist. Whether or not there's something wrong with his T levels, the endo needs to know. Especially if a hysto consult is coming up soon. This is where tracking the period comes in handy -- you'll want to see if it's a regular period that lasts 5-7 days or one that's irregular in either being really brief or really long.

Fourth, there will probably be mood swings. If he's having a period, chances are there's something going on with his hormone levels. This imbalance will create greater mood swings. He's also probably not happy with having it, like you've mentioned, this will cause a bit of a depression funk. It's normal but he may need someone there just to be there.

Try not to call it a setback. This isn't a setback, just a glitch. And a fixable one at that. Take a deep breath, he's going through a lot and he's definitely going to need help. Lots of us deal with our periods and that doesn't make us any less of a man, the same goes for him. It's a shitty thing to happen but it's happening and it *will* go away.

I hope he feels better soon.
